q: A host has the address 172.16.37.200/20. What is its network address?
exp: /20 gives mask 255.255.240.0. Third octet 37 = 00100101; ANDing with 11110000 gives 00100000 = 32, so the network is 172.16.32.0.

q: What is the minimum length of a TCP header (without options)?
exp: The TCP header has 20 bytes of mandatory fields; options can extend it up to 60 bytes.

q: How many parity (check) bits are needed in a Hamming code to protect 11 data bits against single-bit errors?
exp: Need 2ʳ ≥ m + r + 1. For r = 3: 8 ≥ 15 fails; for r = 4: 16 ≥ 16 holds. So r = 4.

q: Which problem is typically associated with distance vector routing protocols?
exp: Slow propagation of bad news in distance vector protocols causes the count-to-infinity problem.

q:
Statement I: In CSMA/CD a station keeps listening to the channel while it is transmitting.
Statement II: After a collision, Ethernet stations wait for a random time chosen by binary exponential backoff.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true, Statement II is false
Statement I is false, Statement II is true
exp: CSMA/CD detects collisions by monitoring the medium during transmission and uses binary exponential backoff for retransmission.

q: In an ARP request, the destination MAC address in the Ethernet frame is
options: the MAC address of the default gateway
the MAC address of the target host, already known
exp: The sender does not yet know the target MAC, so the request is broadcast to the whole LAN; only the owner of the IP replies, by unicast.

q: A voice signal of bandwidth 4 kHz is digitised by PCM at the Nyquist sampling rate with 8 bits per sample. What is the bit rate?
exp: Nyquist rate = 2 x 4 kHz = 8000 samples/s; 8000 x 8 bits = 64,000 bps.

q: The Protocol Data Unit (PDU) at the data link layer is called a:
exp: Data link layer PDUs are frames; transport has segments, network has packets, physical has bits.

q: What is the broadcast address of the subnet to which the host 192.168.1.130/26 belongs?
exp: /26 gives blocks of 64: 128–191. The host lies in 192.168.1.128/26 whose broadcast address is 192.168.1.191.

q: A Selective Repeat protocol uses 4-bit sequence numbers. What is the maximum window size?
exp: For Selective Repeat, the maximum window is 2ⁿ⁻¹ = 2³ = 8.

q: What is the range of well-known port numbers?
exp: Well-known ports are 0–1023, registered ports 1024–49151 and dynamic/private ports 49152–65535.

q: Admission control, in which the network refuses new connections when it is already heavily loaded, is an example of
options: flow control at the data link layer
exp: Open-loop schemes prevent congestion by design or policy before it occurs; closed-loop schemes react to feedback (choke packets, backpressure, ECN).

q: A noisy channel of 3000 Hz bandwidth has a signal-to-noise ratio of 1023 (linear). What is the Shannon capacity?
Which switching technique reserves a dedicated end-to-end path for the whole duration of the communication?
exp: Circuit switching sets up and holds a dedicated path between the two endpoints until the call ends.

q: Which HTTP status code indicates that the requested resource was not found?
exp: 404 means Not Found; 403 is Forbidden, 500 is Internal Server Error and 301 is Moved Permanently.

q: A TCP sender in slow start begins with cwnd = 1 MSS and receives all acknowledgements correctly, with ssthresh very large. What is cwnd after four successful round trips?
exp: In slow start cwnd doubles every RTT: 1 → 2 → 4 → 8 → 16.

q: Which of the following is the correct shortened form of the IPv6 address 2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:ff00:0042:8329?
exp: Leading zeros are dropped and one run of all-zero groups is replaced by '::', giving 2001:db8::ff00:42:8329.

q: In an SMTP session, which command specifies the recipient of the message?
exp: SMTP dialogue: HELO/EHLO, MAIL FROM (sender), RCPT TO (recipient), DATA (body ending with a dot line), QUIT.

q: Two 8-bit words 10110011 and 01101100 are added using one's complement arithmetic and the sum is complemented to form the checksum. What is the checksum?
exp: 179 + 108 = 287 = 1 0001 1111; wrapping the carry gives 00100000; its complement is 11011111.

q: Which topology uses a single backbone cable terminated at both ends to which all nodes are connected?
exp: A bus topology uses one shared backbone cable with terminators at each end.

q: Eight PCs are each connected to a different port of an 8-port switch. How many collision domains exist?
exp: Each switch port is its own collision domain, so there are 8 (while there is just one broadcast domain).

q: An organisation has 192.168.5.0/24 and needs at least 6 equal-sized subnets. What is the maximum number of usable hosts in each subnet?
exp: Six subnets need 3 borrowed bits (8 subnets), leaving 5 host bits: 2⁵ − 2 = 30.

q: Which DNS record type maps a host name to an IPv4 address?
exp: The A record holds the IPv4 address of a host; AAAA holds IPv6.

q: Why is UDP preferred over TCP for real-time voice calls?
options: It guarantees delivery of every packet
It avoids connection set-up and retransmission delays that harm real-time flow
exp: Real-time voice tolerates some loss but not delay, so UDP's low overhead and no retransmission suit it.

q: Which statement about FTP is correct?
options: It uses a persistent control connection and a separate data connection for each transfer
It uses only one UDP connection for both commands and data
It encrypts the user name and password by default
It does not need a login in its default form
exp: FTP has a control connection (port 21) kept for the session and data connections (port 20 in active mode) per transfer. TFTP is the one over UDP without login.

q: For pure ALOHA with frame time T, the vulnerable time of a frame is:
exp: A frame can collide with any frame sent in the interval T before or T after it, so vulnerable time is 2T.

q: In a network, the link costs are A–B = 4, A–C = 2, C–B = 1, B–D = 5, C–D = 8 and D–E = 3. What is the shortest-path cost from A to E?
Which OSI layer is responsible for dialog control and synchronization using checkpoints?
exp: The session layer manages dialogs and inserts synchronization points (checkpoints) in a data stream.

q: A signal travels 2000 km through a medium at 2 × 10⁸ m/s. What is the propagation delay?
Which of the following is a private IPv4 address?
A block code has a minimum Hamming distance of 5. How many errors can it correct?
exp: Correctable errors = ⌊(dmin − 1)/2⌋ = 2 (it can detect up to 4).

q: A Go-Back-N sender transmits frames 0 to 7. Frame 3 is lost but frames 4 to 7 reach the receiver. After the timeout, how many frames are retransmitted?
exp: Go-Back-N resends the lost frame and all that followed it: frames 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 = 5 frames.

q: Which e-mail retrieval protocol keeps messages on the server and synchronises mailbox folders across several devices?
exp: IMAP leaves mail on the server and maintains mailbox state for multiple clients; SMTP only sends mail.

q: Which statement about SMTP is correct?
options: It is a pull protocol used by users to read mail from the mailbox
It keeps messages on the server and synchronises folders
It is a push protocol used to send and relay mail between servers over TCP port 25
exp: SMTP pushes mail from client to server and server to server. Retrieval is done by POP3 or IMAP.

q: Which of the following is NOT an application layer protocol?
exp: ICMP works at the network (Internet) layer; HTTP, DNS and SMTP are application layer protocols.
